"""Tools: a wizard in a modal that generates one output on demand."""
import asyncio

from antioch.dom import DOM
from antioch.elements import Div, Input, Option, Select
from antioch.event import when
from antioch.macros import Modal

from ui_lib import (
    CheckboxGroup, TabItem, TabView, Wizard, WizardPanel, labeled,
    set_select_options,
)

from .config import (
    BIVARIATE_METRICS, DEFAULT_GRID, DENSITY_METHODS, GRID_SIZES, LAYOUTS,
    DEFAULT_POINT_SIZE, GRAIN_WEIGHTINGS, METRICS, MDS_TYPES,
    MIXTURE_METRICS, MIXTURE_TRIALS, SCATTER_LAYOUTS, SCATTER_SIZES,
    SIGMA_LEVELS, TERNARY_TOTAL, TOOLS, VIEWS,
)
from .dataset import detect_columns, numeric_columns, sample_names
from .distributions import build_distribution
from .errors import error_box
from .matrices import build_matrix
from .mds_plot import build_mds
from .mixture import build_mixture
from .pca_axes import build_pca_axes
from .scatter import build_scatter
from .ternary_plot import build_ternary
from .bivariate_plot import build_bivariate
from .bivariate_matrix import build_bivariate_matrix
from .bivariate_mds import build_bivariate_mds
from .bivariate_mixture import build_bivariate_mixture

MODAL_STYLE = {"max-width": "840px", "width": "92vw", "min-width": "0"}


class Tool:
    """
    One entry in the toolbar.

    Owns its modal + wizard, reads the current spreadsheet when submitted, and
    hands each selected dimension to `build`. Several dimensions produce one
    tabbed output with a tab each.
    """

    # Shared numeric option rows, in display order. A tool can take a subset;
    # the bivariate tools drop bin size (they have a grid, not bins) and the
    # single bandwidth (they need one per axis).
    ALL_NUMERIC_ROWS = ("bin_size", "density", "sigma", "bandwidth")

    def __init__(self, key, label, submit_text, option_rows, min_samples,
                 build, read_extra, get_rows, gallery, overlay, on_close=None,
                 sync_extra=None, validate_extra=None,
                 numeric_rows=ALL_NUMERIC_ROWS,
                 dimension_hint="Several dimensions produce one tabbed output, "
                                "a tab each",
                 numeric_dimensions_only=False,
                 use_dimensions=True):
        self.key = key
        self.label = label
        self._min_samples = min_samples
        self._build = build
        self._read_extra = read_extra
        self._get_rows = get_rows
        self._gallery = gallery
        self._overlay = overlay
        self._on_close = on_close
        # Tools whose options depend on the data (a sink picker, say) refresh
        # them here; validate_extra reports a problem the wizard should show.
        self._sync_extra = sync_extra
        self._validate_extra = validate_extra
        self._numeric_rows = numeric_rows
        self._dimension_hint = dimension_hint
        # Density grids need two numeric axes, so those tools never offer a
        # categorical dimension rather than failing once it is submitted.
        self._numeric_dimensions_only = numeric_dimensions_only
        # A tool that names its dimensions some other way — a ternary plot
        # assigns three of them to named apexes — drops the panel entirely
        # rather than showing a checklist that means nothing.
        self._use_dimensions = use_dimensions

        self._title_input = Input("text", placeholder=f"e.g. {label} of size",
                                  style={"width": "260px"})
        self._samples = CheckboxGroup(empty_text="No samples in the spreadsheet")
        self._dimensions = CheckboxGroup(
            empty_text=("No numeric dimensions in the spreadsheet"
                        if numeric_dimensions_only
                        else "No dimensions in the spreadsheet"),
            on_change=lambda values: self._update_option_visibility(),
        )
        # Dimensions holding numbers. Binning, PDPs and KDEs mean nothing for
        # a categorical dimension, so their options are hidden for one.
        self._numeric_columns = set()
        self._bin_size = Input("number", placeholder="auto", style={"width": "90px"})
        self._density = _select(DENSITY_METHODS)
        self._sigma_in = _select(SIGMA_LEVELS)
        self._bandwidth = Input("number", placeholder="auto", style={"width": "90px"})

        self.wizard = self._make_wizard(submit_text, option_rows)
        self.modal = self._make_modal()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- construction

    def _numeric_option_rows(self):
        """
        Option rows that only make sense for numeric dimensions.

        Kept as attributes so _update_option_visibility can show and hide them;
        a bin width or a KDE bandwidth over "quartz, feldspar, mica" is
        meaningless, and offering it invites a nonsense setting.
        """
        available = {
            "bin_size": labeled(
                "Bin size", self._bin_size,
                "Blank picks a round width automatically"),
            "density": labeled(
                "Density method", self._density,
                "How PDF and CDF curves are built; histograms always bin"),
            "sigma": labeled(
                "Uncertainty level", self._sigma_in,
                "For uncertainty columns that don't say; a '1s' or '2s' header "
                "overrides it"),
            "bandwidth": labeled(
                "KDE bandwidth", self._bandwidth,
                "Blank uses Silverman's rule on the pooled samples"),
        }
        self._rows = {key: available[key] for key in self._numeric_rows}
        self._density.on('change', lambda e: self._update_option_visibility())

        rows = list(self._rows.values())
        self._update_option_visibility()
        return rows

    def _update_option_visibility(self):
        """Show the numeric-only rows only when they apply to what's selected."""
        if not hasattr(self, '_rows'):
            return  # rows not built yet

        selected = self._dimensions.values()
        if selected:
            numeric = any(d in self._numeric_columns for d in selected)
        else:
            # Nothing chosen yet: go by whether the spreadsheet has any numbers.
            numeric = bool(self._numeric_columns)

        is_kde = self._density.value == "kde"
        visibility = {
            "bin_size": numeric,
            "density": numeric,
            "sigma": numeric and not is_kde,
            "bandwidth": numeric and is_kde,
        }
        for key, row in self._rows.items():
            row.style.display = "block" if visibility[key] else "none"

    def _make_wizard(self, submit_text, option_rows):
        plural = "s" if self._min_samples != 1 else ""
        dimension_panel = WizardPanel("Dimensions", Div(
            labeled("Dimensions", self._dimensions.element,
                    self._dimension_hint),
        ), "Choose which dimensions of the sample set to graph.")

        panels = [
            WizardPanel("Samples", Div(
                labeled("Output title", self._title_input,
                        "Optional; names the entry and its SVG file"),
                labeled("Samples", self._samples.element,
                        f"Choose at least {self._min_samples} sample{plural}"),
            ), f"Choose the samples to include in the {self.label.lower()}."),
            WizardPanel("Options", Div(
                *option_rows,
                *self._numeric_option_rows(),
            ), "Configure how the distributions are computed."),
        ]
        if self._use_dimensions:
            panels.insert(1, dimension_panel)

        # The modal supplies the title bar and the curtain, so the wizard is
        # built without its own header.
        wizard = Wizard(submit_text=submit_text, panels=panels)
        wizard.element.style.update({
            "margin-top": "0", "border": "none", "border-radius": "0",
        })

        @when(wizard.events.submit)
        def on_submit(sender, *args):
            self._submit()

        return wizard

    def _make_modal(self):
        modal = Modal(title=self.label, modal_style=MODAL_STYLE)
        modal.set_content(self.wizard.element)
        DOM.add(modal.element)

        @when(modal.events.close)
        def on_close(sender, *args):
            if self._on_close:
                self._on_close(self)

        return modal

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- state

    def open(self):
        self.modal.open()
        return self

    def sync_options(self, rows):
        """Keep the sample/dimension choices in step with the spreadsheet."""
        sample_col, _, dimensions = detect_columns(rows)
        names = sample_names(rows, sample_col)
        self._numeric_columns = numeric_columns(rows, dimensions)
        if self._numeric_dimensions_only:
            dimensions = [d for d in dimensions if d in self._numeric_columns]
        self._samples.set_options(names)
        self._dimensions.set_options(dimensions)
        self._update_option_visibility()
        if self._sync_extra:
            self._sync_extra(names, dimensions, self._numeric_columns)
        return self

    def _current_bin_size(self):
        try:
            size = float(self._bin_size.value)
            return size if size > 0 else None
        except ValueError:
            return None

    def _current_bandwidth(self):
        try:
            width = float(self._bandwidth.value)
            return width if width > 0 else None
        except ValueError:
            return None

    def read_options(self):
        opts = {
            "title": self._title_input.value.strip(),
            "samples": self._samples.values(),
            "dimensions": self._dimensions.values() if self._use_dimensions else [],
            "bin_size": self._current_bin_size(),
            "density": self._density.value,
            "sigma_in": float(self._sigma_in.value or 1),
            "bandwidth": self._current_bandwidth(),
        }
        opts.update(self._read_extra())
        return opts

    def _validation_error(self, opts):
        if len(opts["samples"]) < self._min_samples:
            plural = "s" if self._min_samples != 1 else ""
            return (f"{self.label} needs at least {self._min_samples} sample{plural}; "
                    f"{len(opts['samples'])} selected.")
        if self._use_dimensions and not opts["dimensions"]:
            return "Select at least one dimension."
        if self._validate_extra:
            return self._validate_extra(opts)
        return None

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- generation

    def _submit(self):
        opts = self.read_options()
        problem = self._validation_error(opts)
        if problem:
            self.wizard.set_status(problem)
            return

        self.wizard.set_status("")
        self.modal.close()
        asyncio.ensure_future(self._run(opts))

    async def _run(self, opts):
        # Building is synchronous and can take seconds (MDS especially), which
        # freezes the UI thread — so the curtain goes up first and
        # LoadingOverlay.run waits for it to paint before starting.
        try:
            charts = await self._overlay.run(
                lambda: self._generate(opts), f"Building {self.label.lower()}…"
            )
        except Exception as e:
            # ensure_future would otherwise swallow this into a console the
            # user can't reach on a phone.
            self._gallery.add(opts["title"] or self.label,
                              error_box(f"{self.label} failed", e), [])
            return
        # Sized while the gallery was behind the curtain; re-fit now.
        for _, chart in charts:
            chart.resize()

    def _generate(self, opts):
        rows = self._get_rows()
        sample_col, _, _ = detect_columns(rows)
        charts = []
        contents = []

        # Three shapes of output. A tool that names its dimensions elsewhere
        # (ternary picks three apexes) builds once and ignores the target; a
        # combining tool takes the whole list at once; everything else gets one
        # build, and so one tab, per dimension.
        if not self._use_dimensions:
            targets, titles = [None], []
        elif opts.get("combine_dimensions"):
            targets, titles = [opts["dimensions"]], []
        else:
            targets, titles = list(opts["dimensions"]), list(opts["dimensions"])

        for target in targets:
            label = f"'{target}'" if titles else f"the {self.label.lower()}"
            try:
                contents.append(self._build(charts, rows, sample_col, target, opts))
            except Exception as e:
                contents.append(error_box(f"Could not build {label}", e))

        tabview = None
        if len(contents) == 1:
            body = contents[0]
        else:
            tabview = TabView(tabs=[
                TabItem(title, content)
                for title, content in zip(titles, contents)
            ])
            body = tabview.element

            @when(tabview.events.change)
            def on_dimension_tab(sender, *args):
                # Plots sized while their tab was hidden need a re-fit
                for _, chart in charts:
                    chart.resize()

        self._gallery.add(opts["title"] or self.label, body, charts, tabview)
        return charts


def _select(choices, label_of=lambda v: v):
    return Select(*[Option(label_of(v), value=k) for k, v in choices.items()])


def build_tools(get_rows, gallery, overlay, on_close=None, set_rows=None):
    """Every tool, keyed the way dashboard.config.TOOL_MENU refers to them."""
    shared = {"get_rows": get_rows, "gallery": gallery,
              "overlay": overlay, "on_close": on_close}
    tools = {}

    # Distributions
    view = _select(VIEWS, lambda v: v["label"])
    layout = _select(LAYOUTS)
    tools["distributions"] = Tool(
        "distributions", TOOLS["distributions"], "Create distribution plots",
        option_rows=[
            labeled("View", view, "Histogram counts, or normalized PDF / CDF"),
            labeled("Layout", layout,
                    "Overlay samples on one plot, or stack one per sample"),
        ],
        min_samples=1,
        build=build_distribution,
        read_extra=lambda: {"view": view.value, "layout": layout.value},
        **shared,
    )

    # Comparison matrices
    matrix_metric = _select(METRICS, lambda m: m["label"])
    tools["matrix"] = Tool(
        "matrix", TOOLS["matrix"], "Create comparison matrices",
        option_rows=[
            labeled("Comparison metric", matrix_metric,
                    "Statistic computed for every pair of samples"),
        ],
        min_samples=2,
        build=build_matrix,
        read_extra=lambda: {"metric": matrix_metric.value},
        **shared,
    )

    # MDS
    mds_metric = _select(METRICS, lambda m: m["label"])
    mds_type = _select(MDS_TYPES)
    shepard = Input("checkbox")
    tools["mds"] = Tool(
        "mds", TOOLS["mds"], "Create MDS plots",
        option_rows=[
            labeled("Comparison metric", mds_metric,
                    "Used to build the dissimilarity matrix"),
            labeled("MDS type", mds_type,
                    "Non-metric preserves rank order; metric preserves distances"),
            labeled("Shepard plot", shepard,
                    "Diagnostic comparing dissimilarities to MDS distances"),
        ],
        min_samples=3,
        build=build_mds,
        read_extra=lambda: {
            "metric": mds_metric.value,
            "mds_type": mds_type.value,
            "shepard": shepard._dom_element.checked,
        },
        **shared,
    )

    # Mixture model
    sink = Select()
    mixture_metric = _select(MIXTURE_METRICS, lambda m: m["label"])
    trials = Select(*[Option(f"{n:,}", value=str(n)) for n in MIXTURE_TRIALS])
    trials.value = str(MIXTURE_TRIALS[2])

    def validate_mixture(opts):
        if not opts["sink"]:
            return "Choose a sink sample."
        if opts["sink"] not in opts["samples"]:
            return f"The sink '{opts['sink']}' is not among the selected samples."
        # The sink is one of the selected samples, so unmixing it needs two
        # more alongside it.
        if len(opts["samples"]) < 3:
            return "Select the sink plus at least two source samples."
        return None

    tools["mixture"] = Tool(
        "mixture", TOOLS["mixture"], "Create mixture model",
        option_rows=[
            labeled("Sink sample", sink,
                    "The mixed sample; every other selected sample is a source"),
            labeled("Comparison metric", mixture_metric,
                    "Scores each trial's modelled curve against the sink"),
            labeled("Trials", trials,
                    "Random source configurations to try; more is slower but steadier"),
        ],
        min_samples=3,
        build=build_mixture,
        read_extra=lambda: {
            "sink": sink.value,
            "metric": mixture_metric.value,
            "trials": int(trials.value),
        },
        sync_extra=lambda names, dimensions, numeric: set_select_options(
            sink, names, empty_text="No samples"),
        validate_extra=validate_mixture,
        **shared,
    )

    # Scatterplot — the raw grains, not a distribution of them.
    scatter_x = Select()
    scatter_layout = _select(SCATTER_LAYOUTS)
    scatter_color = Input("checkbox")
    scatter_color._dom_element.checked = True
    scatter_size = _select(SCATTER_SIZES)
    scatter_size.value = DEFAULT_POINT_SIZE

    def validate_scatter(opts):
        if not opts.get("x_dimension"):
            return "Choose an x dimension."
        if all(d == opts["x_dimension"] for d in opts["dimensions"]):
            return ("The x dimension is the only one checked; choose a "
                    "different y dimension.")
        return None

    tools["scatter"] = Tool(
        "scatter", TOOLS["scatter"], "Create scatterplots",
        option_rows=[
            labeled("X dimension", scatter_x,
                    "Plotted against each dimension checked on the previous step"),
            labeled("Colour by sample", scatter_color,
                    "Each sample gets its own colour and marker shape"),
            labeled("Layout", scatter_layout,
                    "Overlay every sample, or give each its own panel on "
                    "shared axes"),
            labeled("Point size", scatter_size,
                    "Smaller reads better where grains pile up"),
        ],
        min_samples=1,
        build=build_scatter,
        read_extra=lambda: {
            "x_dimension": scatter_x.value,
            "layout": scatter_layout.value,
            "color_by_sample": scatter_color._dom_element.checked,
            "point_size": int(scatter_size.value or DEFAULT_POINT_SIZE),
        },
        sync_extra=lambda names, dimensions, numeric: set_select_options(
            scatter_x, [d for d in dimensions if d in numeric],
            empty_text="No numeric dimensions"),
        validate_extra=validate_scatter,
        # A scatter draws the measurements themselves; there is nothing to bin,
        # smooth or assign an uncertainty to.
        numeric_rows=(),
        numeric_dimensions_only=True,
        dimension_hint="Each becomes the y axis against the x dimension below",
        **shared,
    )

    # Ternary — three parts of a whole, one point per grain.
    apex_a, apex_b, apex_c = Select(), Select(), Select()
    ternary_color = Input("checkbox")
    ternary_color._dom_element.checked = True
    ternary_centroids = Input("checkbox")
    ternary_size = _select(SCATTER_SIZES)
    ternary_size.value = DEFAULT_POINT_SIZE

    def validate_ternary(opts):
        apexes = [opts.get("apex_a"), opts.get("apex_b"), opts.get("apex_c")]
        if not all(apexes):
            return "Choose all three apex dimensions."
        if len(set(apexes)) < 3:
            return "The three apexes must be different dimensions."
        return None

    def sync_ternary(names, dimensions, numeric):
        # Only numeric columns can be a part of a whole.
        usable = [d for d in dimensions if d in numeric]
        for select in (apex_a, apex_b, apex_c):
            set_select_options(select, usable, empty_text="No numeric dimensions")
        # Open on three different columns rather than three copies of the
        # first, so the plot is valid before anything is touched.
        for select, value in zip((apex_a, apex_b, apex_c), usable[:3]):
            if not select.value or select.value not in usable:
                select.value = value

    tools["ternary"] = Tool(
        "ternary", TOOLS["ternary"], "Create ternary plot",
        option_rows=[
            labeled("Top apex", apex_a, "The component plotted at the peak"),
            labeled("Lower-left apex", apex_b, ""),
            labeled("Lower-right apex", apex_c, ""),
            labeled("Colour by sample", ternary_color,
                    "Each sample gets its own colour and marker shape"),
            labeled("Mark sample means", ternary_centroids,
                    "A star at each sample's mean composition, with a table"),
            labeled("Point size", ternary_size,
                    "Smaller reads better where grains pile up"),
        ],
        min_samples=1,
        build=build_ternary,
        read_extra=lambda: {
            "apex_a": apex_a.value,
            "apex_b": apex_b.value,
            "apex_c": apex_c.value,
            "color_by_sample": ternary_color._dom_element.checked,
            "show_centroids": ternary_centroids._dom_element.checked,
            "point_size": int(ternary_size.value or DEFAULT_POINT_SIZE),
        },
        sync_extra=sync_ternary,
        validate_extra=validate_ternary,
        # Each grain is closed to a constant sum; there is nothing to bin or
        # smooth, and the three apexes replace the dimension checklist.
        numeric_rows=(),
        use_dimensions=False,
        **shared,
    )

    # PCA axes — reduces many variables to PC1/PC2 per grain and writes them
    # back as spreadsheet columns for the other tools to consume.
    axes_weighting = _select(GRAIN_WEIGHTINGS)
    axes_scree = Input("checkbox")

    def validate_axes(opts):
        usable = [d for d in opts["dimensions"] if d not in ("PC1", "PC2")]
        if len(usable) < 2:
            return "Choose at least two variables to reduce."
        return None

    tools["pca"] = Tool(
        "pca", TOOLS["pca"], "Add PC1 and PC2 columns",
        option_rows=[
            labeled("Weighting", axes_weighting,
                    "Stops a sample with many analyses from setting the axis "
                    "for everyone"),
            labeled("Scree plot", axes_scree,
                    "Shows how much is lost by keeping only two axes"),
        ],
        min_samples=1,
        build=lambda charts, rows, sample_col, dims, opts: build_pca_axes(
            charts, rows, sample_col, dims, opts, set_rows=set_rows),
        read_extra=lambda: {
            "grain_weighting": axes_weighting.value,
            "scree": axes_scree._dom_element.checked,
            # Every chosen variable goes into one fit, so there is one output.
            "combine_dimensions": True,
        },
        validate_extra=validate_axes,
        numeric_rows=(),
        numeric_dimensions_only=True,
        dimension_hint="The variables to reduce; all go into one fit",
        **shared,
    )

    _add_bivariate_tools(tools, shared)
    return tools


def _add_bivariate_tools(tools, shared):
    """
    The three tools built on 2-D density grids.

    Each pairs one x dimension against every checked dimension, so the
    per-dimension tab loop still applies: a tab per y variable, all against the
    same x. That matches how paired data is actually read — age against Hf,
    against Ti, against Th/U.
    """
    # Bin size means nothing on a grid, and one bandwidth cannot cover two axes.
    numeric_rows = ("density", "sigma")
    dimension_hint = "Each becomes the y axis against the x dimension below"

    def axis_controls():
        """An x-dimension picker plus its own per-axis bandwidths and grid."""
        x_dimension = Select()
        grid = _select(GRID_SIZES)
        grid.value = DEFAULT_GRID
        x_bandwidth = Input("number", placeholder="auto", style={"width": "90px"})
        y_bandwidth = Input("number", placeholder="auto", style={"width": "90px"})
        return x_dimension, grid, x_bandwidth, y_bandwidth

    def axis_rows(x_dimension, grid, x_bandwidth, y_bandwidth):
        return [
            labeled("X dimension", x_dimension,
                    "Plotted against each dimension checked on the previous step"),
            labeled("Grid resolution", grid,
                    "Points per axis; cost grows with the square"),
            labeled("X bandwidth", x_bandwidth,
                    "Blank uses Silverman's rule; ignored when uncertainties are used"),
            labeled("Y bandwidth", y_bandwidth,
                    "Blank uses Silverman's rule; ignored when uncertainties are used"),
        ]

    def axis_options(x_dimension, grid, x_bandwidth, y_bandwidth):
        return {
            "x_dimension": x_dimension.value,
            "grid": int(grid.value or DEFAULT_GRID),
            "x_bandwidth": _positive(x_bandwidth.value),
            "y_bandwidth": _positive(y_bandwidth.value),
        }

    def sync_axis(x_dimension):
        def sync(names, dimensions, numeric):
            # A density grid needs two numeric axes, so a categorical column is
            # not a candidate for x.
            set_select_options(x_dimension, [d for d in dimensions if d in numeric],
                               empty_text="No numeric dimensions")
        return sync

    def validate_axis(x_dimension):
        def validate(opts):
            if not opts.get("x_dimension"):
                return "Choose an x dimension."
            if all(d == opts["x_dimension"] for d in opts["dimensions"]):
                return ("The x dimension is the only one checked; choose a "
                        "different y dimension.")
            return None
        return validate

    # Bivariate density
    x_dim, grid, x_bw, y_bw = axis_controls()
    show_points = Input("checkbox")
    tools["bivariate"] = Tool(
        "bivariate", TOOLS["bivariate"], "Create density plots",
        option_rows=axis_rows(x_dim, grid, x_bw, y_bw) + [
            labeled("Overlay grains", show_points,
                    "Draw the raw measurements over the density"),
        ],
        min_samples=1,
        build=build_bivariate,
        read_extra=lambda: {
            **axis_options(x_dim, grid, x_bw, y_bw),
            "show_points": show_points._dom_element.checked,
        },
        sync_extra=sync_axis(x_dim),
        validate_extra=validate_axis(x_dim),
        numeric_rows=numeric_rows,
        dimension_hint=dimension_hint,
        numeric_dimensions_only=True,
        **shared,
    )

    # Bivariate comparison matrices
    matrix_x, matrix_grid, matrix_x_bw, matrix_y_bw = axis_controls()
    matrix_metric = _select(BIVARIATE_METRICS, lambda m: m["label"])
    tools["bivariate_matrix"] = Tool(
        "bivariate_matrix", TOOLS["bivariate_matrix"], "Create comparison matrices",
        option_rows=axis_rows(matrix_x, matrix_grid, matrix_x_bw, matrix_y_bw) + [
            labeled("Comparison metric", matrix_metric,
                    "Two-dimensional measure computed for every pair of samples"),
        ],
        min_samples=2,
        build=build_bivariate_matrix,
        read_extra=lambda: {
            **axis_options(matrix_x, matrix_grid, matrix_x_bw, matrix_y_bw),
            "metric": matrix_metric.value,
        },
        sync_extra=sync_axis(matrix_x),
        validate_extra=validate_axis(matrix_x),
        numeric_rows=numeric_rows,
        dimension_hint=dimension_hint,
        numeric_dimensions_only=True,
        **shared,
    )

    # Bivariate MDS
    mds_x, mds_grid, mds_x_bw, mds_y_bw = axis_controls()
    mds_metric = _select(BIVARIATE_METRICS, lambda m: m["label"])
    mds_type = _select(MDS_TYPES)
    shepard = Input("checkbox")
    tools["bivariate_mds"] = Tool(
        "bivariate_mds", TOOLS["bivariate_mds"], "Create MDS plots",
        option_rows=axis_rows(mds_x, mds_grid, mds_x_bw, mds_y_bw) + [
            labeled("Comparison metric", mds_metric,
                    "Used to build the 2D dissimilarity matrix"),
            labeled("MDS type", mds_type,
                    "Non-metric preserves rank order; metric preserves distances"),
            labeled("Shepard plot", shepard,
                    "Diagnostic comparing dissimilarities to MDS distances"),
        ],
        min_samples=3,
        build=build_bivariate_mds,
        read_extra=lambda: {
            **axis_options(mds_x, mds_grid, mds_x_bw, mds_y_bw),
            "metric": mds_metric.value,
            "mds_type": mds_type.value,
            "shepard": shepard._dom_element.checked,
        },
        sync_extra=sync_axis(mds_x),
        validate_extra=validate_axis(mds_x),
        numeric_rows=numeric_rows,
        dimension_hint=dimension_hint,
        numeric_dimensions_only=True,
        **shared,
    )

    # Bivariate mixture model
    mix_x, mix_grid, mix_x_bw, mix_y_bw = axis_controls()
    mix_sink = Select()
    mix_metric = _select(MIXTURE_METRICS, lambda m: m["label"])
    mix_trials = Select(*[Option(f"{n:,}", value=str(n)) for n in MIXTURE_TRIALS])
    mix_trials.value = str(MIXTURE_TRIALS[2])

    def sync_mixture(names, dimensions, numeric):
        set_select_options(mix_x, [d for d in dimensions if d in numeric],
                           empty_text="No numeric dimensions")
        set_select_options(mix_sink, names, empty_text="No samples")

    def validate_mixture_2d(opts):
        problem = validate_axis(mix_x)(opts)
        if problem:
            return problem
        if not opts.get("sink"):
            return "Choose a sink sample."
        if opts["sink"] not in opts["samples"]:
            return f"The sink '{opts['sink']}' is not among the selected samples."
        if len(opts["samples"]) < 3:
            return "Select the sink plus at least two source samples."
        return None

    tools["bivariate_mixture"] = Tool(
        "bivariate_mixture", TOOLS["bivariate_mixture"], "Create mixture model",
        option_rows=axis_rows(mix_x, mix_grid, mix_x_bw, mix_y_bw) + [
            labeled("Sink sample", mix_sink,
                    "The mixed sample; every other selected sample is a source"),
            labeled("Comparison metric", mix_metric,
                    "Scores each trial's modelled density against the sink"),
            labeled("Trials", mix_trials,
                    "Random source configurations to try"),
        ],
        min_samples=3,
        build=build_bivariate_mixture,
        read_extra=lambda: {
            **axis_options(mix_x, mix_grid, mix_x_bw, mix_y_bw),
            "sink": mix_sink.value,
            "metric": mix_metric.value,
            "trials": int(mix_trials.value),
        },
        sync_extra=sync_mixture,
        validate_extra=validate_mixture_2d,
        numeric_rows=numeric_rows,
        dimension_hint=dimension_hint,
        numeric_dimensions_only=True,
        **shared,
    )


def _positive(value):
    """A positive float from a number input, or None when blank or invalid."""
    try:
        number = float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return number if number > 0 else None

"""The MDS tool's output: the ordination map and its optional Shepard plot."""
import numpy as np

from antioch.elements import Div, P

from plot_lib import line_trace, marker_trace, series_color
from sed_stats import mds

from .config import METRICS, MDS_TYPES
from .dataset import series_for
from .plots import make_plot

CAPTION_STYLE = {"font-size": "13px", "color": "#555", "margin": "0 0 6px 0"}


def build_mds(charts, rows, sample_col, dimension, opts):
    metric = opts["metric"]
    _, series = series_for(rows, sample_col, dimension,
                           mds.expected_form(metric), opts)
    if len(series) < 3:
        return P("Need at least three samples with data for MDS.",
                 style={"color": "#6c757d"})

    non_metric = opts["mds_type"] == "non_metric"
    points, stress, matrix, embedding = mds.mds_function(series, metric, non_metric)

    wrapper = Div(
        P(f"{MDS_TYPES[opts['mds_type']]} on {METRICS[metric]['label']} "
          f"dissimilarity — Kruskal stress-1: {stress:.4f}", style=CAPTION_STYLE),
        Div(make_plot(charts, _map_traces(points), f"{dimension} — MDS",
                      "Dimension 1", "Dimension 2",
                      filename=f"{dimension}_mds").element),
    )

    if opts["shepard"]:
        wrapper.add(*_shepard_section(charts, dimension, matrix, embedding,
                                      non_metric, stress))
    return wrapper


def _map_traces(points):
    # Dashed segments joining each sample to its nearest neighbor. A None
    # breaks the line between segments; Plotly reads array entries as values,
    # so a non-numeric entry is simply a gap.
    nn_x, nn_y = [], []
    for point in points:
        if point.nearest_neighbor is not None:
            nn_x.extend([point.x, point.nearest_neighbor[0], None])
            nn_y.extend([point.y, point.nearest_neighbor[1], None])

    traces = []
    if nn_x:
        traces.append({
            "type": "scatter", "mode": "lines", "x": nn_x, "y": nn_y,
            "name": "Nearest neighbor",
            "line": {"color": "#999", "width": 1, "dash": "dash"},
            "connectgaps": False, "hoverinfo": "skip",
        })
    # Points are added after the connectors so they draw on top.
    traces.extend(
        marker_trace([p.x], [p.y], p.label,
                     color=series_color(i, len(points)), labels=[p.label])
        for i, p in enumerate(points)
    )
    return traces


def _shepard_section(charts, dimension, matrix, embedding, non_metric, stress):
    """Caption + plot comparing input dissimilarities to the embedding's distances."""
    shepard = mds.shepard_data(matrix, embedding, non_metric)
    dissimilarities = shepard["dissimilarities"]
    distances = shepard["distances"]
    max_val = float(max(dissimilarities.max(), distances.max())) if len(distances) else 1.0

    traces = [marker_trace(
        [float(d) for d in dissimilarities],
        [float(v) for v in distances],
        "Distances", color="rgba(54, 162, 235, 0.8)", size=7,
    )]
    if shepard["disparities"] is not None:
        order = np.argsort(dissimilarities)
        traces.append(line_trace(
            [float(dissimilarities[i]) for i in order],
            [float(shepard["disparities"][i]) for i in order],
            "Disparities", color="#d62728", markers=False,
        ))
    traces.append({
        "type": "scatter", "mode": "lines",
        "x": [0, max_val], "y": [0, max_val], "name": "1:1",
        "line": {"color": "#000", "width": 1, "dash": "dot"},
    })

    caption = P(f"Shepard plot — R² = {shepard['r2']:.3f}, stress-1 = {stress:.4f}",
                style={**CAPTION_STYLE, "margin": "16px 0 6px 0"})
    plot = Div(make_plot(charts, traces, f"{dimension} — Shepard plot",
                         "Dissimilarities", "Distances / disparities",
                         height=340, filename=f"{dimension}_shepard").element)
    return caption, plot

"""
Building bivariate distributions from spreadsheet rows.

Shared by the three bivariate tools: the density plots, the comparison
matrices and the MDS map all start from the same per-sample grids, which must
sit on one common axis pair for the 2D measures to mean anything.
"""
from antioch.elements import P

from sed_stats.distributions.bivariate import axis_grid, bivariate_density
from sed_stats.distributions.numeric import silverman_bandwidth

from .dataset import paired_by_sample

NOTE_STYLE = {"color": "#6c757d"}

# Silverman is computed on the pooled samples, so every sample is smoothed
# identically; smoothing them differently would put a difference in the metric
# that isn't in the data.


class BivariateSet:
    """
    Every selected sample's density on one shared grid.

    Attributes:
        entries    - [(sample_name, BivariateDistribution), ...]
        x_values, y_values - the shared axes
        used_uncertainties - (x, y) flags: did per-grain uncertainties drive
                             each axis's kernel widths
        x_bandwidth, y_bandwidth - the KDE widths, when they did not
        counts     - {sample: number of paired measurements}
    """

    def __init__(self, entries, x_values, y_values, used_uncertainties,
                 x_bandwidth, y_bandwidth, counts):
        self.entries = entries
        self.x_values = x_values
        self.y_values = y_values
        self.used_uncertainties = used_uncertainties
        self.x_bandwidth = x_bandwidth
        self.y_bandwidth = y_bandwidth
        self.counts = counts

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.entries)

    @property
    def method_note(self):
        """How each axis was smoothed — they can differ."""
        use_x, use_y = self.used_uncertainties
        if use_x and use_y:
            return "each grain spread by its own analytical uncertainty (PDP)"
        if not use_x and not use_y:
            return (f"KDE, bandwidths {self.x_bandwidth:.3g} (x) "
                    f"and {self.y_bandwidth:.3g} (y)")
        if use_x:
            return (f"x from each grain's own uncertainty, "
                    f"y by KDE at bandwidth {self.y_bandwidth:.3g}")
        return (f"x by KDE at bandwidth {self.x_bandwidth:.3g}, "
                f"y from each grain's own uncertainty")


def prepare(rows, sample_col, y_dimension, opts, min_samples=1, purpose="compare"):
    """
    The density set for one y dimension, or a note explaining why there isn't one.

    Every bivariate tool needs the same four checks, and each one is a normal
    thing for a user to hit — an unset axis, a dimension paired with itself, a
    categorical column, too few samples. None of them is an error worth a
    traceback.

    Returns:
        (BivariateSet, None) on success, or (None, element) to render instead
    """
    x_dimension = opts.get("x_dimension")
    if not x_dimension:
        return None, P("Choose an x dimension.", style=NOTE_STYLE)
    if x_dimension == y_dimension:
        return None, P(f"'{y_dimension}' is already the x dimension; pick a "
                       f"different y dimension.", style=NOTE_STYLE)

    try:
        density_set = build_set(rows, sample_col, x_dimension, y_dimension, opts)
    except ValueError:
        # A density grid needs two numeric axes; a categorical column has no
        # position on one.
        return None, P(f"'{y_dimension}' is not numeric, so it cannot be a "
                       f"density axis. Use the Distributions tool for it.",
                       style=NOTE_STYLE)

    if not len(density_set):
        return None, P(f"No paired '{x_dimension}' and '{y_dimension}' values.",
                       style=NOTE_STYLE)
    if len(density_set) < min_samples:
        return None, P(f"Need at least {min_samples} samples with paired values "
                       f"to {purpose}.", style=NOTE_STYLE)

    return density_set, None


def build_set(rows, sample_col, x_dimension, y_dimension, opts) -> BivariateSet:
    """
    Densities for every selected sample over `x_dimension` vs `y_dimension`.

    Uses per-grain uncertainties when the density method is "auto" and the
    spreadsheet actually has them; otherwise falls back to a KDE, since a
    bivariate distribution has no binned form to retreat to.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if either dimension is not numeric
    """
    grouped = paired_by_sample(
        rows, sample_col, x_dimension, y_dimension,
        opts.get("samples"), opts.get("sigma_in", 1.0))
    if not grouped:
        return BivariateSet([], [], [], (False, False), 0.0, 0.0, {})

    pooled_x = [v for entry in grouped.values() for v in entry[0]]
    pooled_y = [v for entry in grouped.values() for v in entry[1]]
    pooled_x_sigma = [s for entry in grouped.values() for s in entry[2]]
    pooled_y_sigma = [s for entry in grouped.values() for s in entry[3]]

    # Decided per axis, not once for the pair. One variable commonly has an
    # uncertainty column and the other does not — age with a "1s" beside it,
    # plotted against a trace element that has none. Treating that as "the pair
    # has uncertainties" would give the second axis a kernel floored to half a
    # grid step, turning its density into a field of near-delta spikes.
    automatic = opts.get("density", "auto") == "auto"
    use_x_sigmas = automatic and any(s > 0 for s in pooled_x_sigma)
    use_y_sigmas = automatic and any(s > 0 for s in pooled_y_sigma)

    x_bandwidth = opts.get("x_bandwidth") or float(silverman_bandwidth(pooled_x))
    y_bandwidth = opts.get("y_bandwidth") or float(silverman_bandwidth(pooled_y))

    # Pad each axis by whatever kernel it will actually be drawn with, so a
    # grain with a large uncertainty is not clipped at the edge.
    grid = int(opts.get("grid", 128))
    x_values = axis_grid(pooled_x, pooled_x_sigma if use_x_sigmas else [x_bandwidth],
                         grid)
    y_values = axis_grid(pooled_y, pooled_y_sigma if use_y_sigmas else [y_bandwidth],
                         grid)

    entries = []
    counts = {}
    for sample, (xs, ys, x_sigmas, y_sigmas) in grouped.items():
        entries.append((sample, bivariate_density(
            xs, ys,
            x_sigmas if use_x_sigmas else x_bandwidth,
            y_sigmas if use_y_sigmas else y_bandwidth,
            x_values, y_values, name=sample)))
        counts[sample] = len(xs)

    return BivariateSet(entries, x_values, y_values,
                        (use_x_sigmas, use_y_sigmas),
                        x_bandwidth, y_bandwidth, counts)

"""
The "Save to Drive" dialog: pick a name and a destination folder.

Replaces a bare `js.prompt`, which could only ask for a name and gave the user
no say in where the file landed — everything went to the root of My Drive.

Choosing the folder through Google's own picker is also what makes writing
into it legal under the `drive.file` scope: the app may write where the user
pointed it, and nowhere else.
"""
import asyncio

from antioch.dom import DOM
from antioch.elements import Div, Input, Label, P, Span
from antioch.event import when
from antioch.macros import Modal

from component_lib.button import ButtonSecondary, ButtonSuccess

MODAL_STYLE = {"max-width": "460px", "width": "92vw"}
ROW_STYLE = {"margin-bottom": "14px"}
LABEL_STYLE = {
    "display": "block", "font-size": "13px", "font-weight": "600",
    "margin-bottom": "5px", "color": "#333",
}
INPUT_STYLE = {
    "width": "100%", "box-sizing": "border-box", "padding": "8px 10px",
    "font-size": "14px", "border": "1px solid #ccc", "border-radius": "4px",
}
FOLDER_ROW_STYLE = {
    "display": "flex", "align-items": "center", "gap": "10px",
    "flex-wrap": "wrap",
}
FOLDER_NAME_STYLE = {
    "font-size": "13px", "color": "#333", "flex": "1", "min-width": "0",
    "overflow": "hidden", "text-overflow": "ellipsis", "white-space": "nowrap",
}
ERROR_STYLE = {"font-size": "13px", "color": "#b00020", "margin": "0 0 10px 0"}
ACTIONS_STYLE = {
    "display": "flex", "justify-content": "flex-end", "gap": "8px",
    "margin-top": "18px",
}

MY_DRIVE = "My Drive"


class SaveDialog:
    """
    Asks for a filename and destination, then hands both back.

    Usage:
        dialog = SaveDialog(session)
        choice = await dialog.ask("plot.svg")
        if choice:                      # None when cancelled
            name, folder_id = choice["name"], choice["folder_id"]
    """

    def __init__(self, session, title="Save to Google Drive"):
        self.session = session
        self._future = None
        self._folder_id = None

        self._name = Input("text", style=INPUT_STYLE)
        self._folder_label = Span(MY_DRIVE, style=FOLDER_NAME_STYLE)
        self._error = P("", style=ERROR_STYLE)
        self._error.style.display = "none"

        choose = ButtonSecondary("Choose folder…", size="small")
        reset = ButtonSecondary("My Drive", size="small")
        cancel = ButtonSecondary("Cancel", size="small")
        save = ButtonSuccess("Save", size="small")

        @when(choose.events.click)
        def on_choose(sender, *args):
            asyncio.ensure_future(self._choose_folder())

        @when(reset.events.click)
        def on_reset(sender, *args):
            self._set_folder(None, MY_DRIVE)

        @when(cancel.events.click)
        def on_cancel(sender, *args):
            self.modal.close()

        @when(save.events.click)
        def on_save(sender, *args):
            self._submit()

        # Enter in the name field is the obvious way to accept this dialog.
        self._name.on("keydown", self._on_key)

        body = Div(
            Div(Label("File name", style=LABEL_STYLE), self._name,
                style=ROW_STYLE),
            Div(Label("Destination", style=LABEL_STYLE),
                Div(self._folder_label, choose, reset, style=FOLDER_ROW_STYLE),
                style=ROW_STYLE),
            self._error,
            Div(cancel, save, style=ACTIONS_STYLE),
        )

        self.modal = Modal(title=title, modal_style=MODAL_STYLE)
        self.modal.set_content(body)
        DOM.add(self.modal.element)

        @when(self.modal.events.close)
        def on_close(sender, *args):
            # Covers the backdrop, the X and Escape, all of which bypass the
            # buttons and would otherwise leave the caller awaiting forever.
            self._finish(None)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- ask

    async def ask(self, suggested_name):
        """
        Show the dialog and wait for the user.

        Returns {"name", "folder_id", "folder_name"} or None if cancelled.
        """
        self._name.value = suggested_name
        self._show_error("")
        self._future = asyncio.get_event_loop().create_future()
        self.modal.open()
        self._focus_name()
        return await self._future

    def _focus_name(self):
        try:
            self._name.dom_element.focus()
            self._name.dom_element.select()
        except Exception:
            # Focus is a convenience; never let it break the dialog.
            pass

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- internals

    def _on_key(self, dom_event):
        if getattr(dom_event, "key", None) == "Enter":
            dom_event.preventDefault()
            self._submit()

    def _set_folder(self, folder_id, folder_name):
        self._folder_id = folder_id
        self._folder_label.set_text(folder_name)

    def _show_error(self, message):
        self._error.set_text(message)
        self._error.style.display = "block" if message else "none"

    async def _choose_folder(self):
        try:
            picked = await self.session.pick_folder()
        except Exception as error:
            self._show_error(str(error))
            return
        if picked:
            self._set_folder(picked["id"], picked["name"])
            self._show_error("")

    def _submit(self):
        name = str(self._name.value or "").strip()
        if not name:
            self._show_error("Give the file a name.")
            return
        self._finish({
            "name": name,
            "folder_id": self._folder_id,
            "folder_name": self._folder_label.dom_element.textContent,
        })
        # Closing fires the modal's close event, which calls _finish(None);
        # that is harmless because the pending future has already been taken.
        self.modal.close()

    def _finish(self, result):
        """Resolve the waiter exactly once, whichever way the dialog ended."""
        future, self._future = self._future, None
        if future is not None and not future.done():
            future.set_result(result)
scripts/dashboard/drive.py:
"""
Sign in with Google, and move spreadsheets between Drive and the grid.

The panel hides itself entirely when no Cloud project is configured (see
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and friends in `config`), so a copy of the app without
credentials has no Google features rather than buttons that cannot work.
"""
import asyncio

from antioch.elements import Button, Div, Span
from antioch.event import when
from antioch.macros.base import Macro
from component_lib.button import ButtonSecondary

from drive_lib import DriveClient, GoogleSession, PICKABLE
from spreadsheet_lib import parse_file, rows_to_csv

from .config import GOOGLE_API_KEY, GOOGLE_APP_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
from .save_dialog import SaveDialog

STATUS_STYLE = {"margin-left": "10px", "font-size": "13px", "color": "#555"}
ERROR_COLOR = "#b00020"
DEFAULT_SAVE_NAME = "sed-stats-data.csv"

# Shown when sign-in succeeded but the Drive checkbox was left unticked on
# Google's consent screen — a valid token that 403s on every file call.
NO_DRIVE_MESSAGE = ("Signed in, but Drive access was not granted. "
                    "Click Sign out, then sign in again and tick the Google "
                    "Drive permission.")

# The account control sits in the dark header bar, so it is styled against that
# rather than reusing the page's buttons, which assume a light background.
ACCOUNT_STYLE = {
    "display": "flex", "align-items": "center", "gap": "10px",
    "margin-left": "auto", "flex-shrink": "0",
}
ACCOUNT_LABEL_STYLE = {
    "font-size": "13px", "color": "#cfd8e3",
    "max-width": "220px", "overflow": "hidden",
    "text-overflow": "ellipsis", "white-space": "nowrap",
}
ACCOUNT_BUTTON_STYLE = {
    "background-color": "transparent", "color": "#fff",
    "border": "1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.4)",
    "padding": "5px 12px", "font-size": "13px", "cursor": "pointer",
    "border-radius": "4px", "white-space": "nowrap",
}
ACCOUNT_BUTTON_HOVER = "rgba(255,255,255,0.15)"


class DrivePanel(Macro):
    """
    Sign-in, "Open from Drive" and "Save to Drive" controls.

    Usage:
        drive = DrivePanel(get_rows=table.get_data)
        DOM.add(drive.element)

        @when(drive.events.data_loaded)
        def on_loaded(sender, rows, filename):
            ...

    Fires `data_loaded(rows, filename)` on a successful open, and
    `error(message)` on any failure.
    """

    def __init__(self, get_rows=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(macro_type="drive_panel", **kwargs)

        self._get_rows = get_rows
        self._email = None
        # Built lazily: the modal mounts itself into the page, and an
        # unconfigured app should add nothing.
        self._dialog = None
        self.session = GoogleSession(
            client_id=GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID,
            api_key=GOOGLE_API_KEY,
            app_id=GOOGLE_APP_ID,
        )
        self.client = DriveClient(self.session)

        # Mirrors SpreadsheetUpload so the app can drive one overlay for both.
        self._create_event('load_start')
        self._create_event('data_loaded')
        self._create_event('error')
        self._create_event('sign_in_change')

        self._init_macro()

    @property
    def configured(self):
        return self.session.configured

    @property
    def dialog(self):
        if self._dialog is None:
            self._dialog = SaveDialog(self.session)
        return self._dialog

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- elements

    def _create_elements(self):
        container = self._register_element(
            'container',
            self._create_container({"display": "inline-flex",
                                    "align-items": "center",
                                    "flex-wrap": "wrap", "gap": "8px"}),
        )
        self._register_element('account', self._account_control())

        if not self.configured:
            # Nothing to sign in to. Leave the container empty and hidden so
            # the surrounding layout collapses around it.
            container.style.display = "none"
            return container

        # Created enabled, then disabled: ButtonPrimary wires its click
        # handler only when it renders in an enabled state, and set_disabled
        # never wires it afterwards, so a button born disabled stays dead.
        open_button = self._register_element(
            'open', ButtonSecondary("Open from Drive", size="small"))
        save_button = self._register_element(
            'save', ButtonSecondary("Save to Drive", size="small"))
        open_button.set_disabled(True)
        save_button.set_disabled(True)
        self._register_element('status', Span("", style=STATUS_STYLE))

        @when(open_button.events.click)
        def on_open(sender, *args):
            asyncio.ensure_future(self._open())

        @when(save_button.events.click)
        def on_save(sender, *args):
            asyncio.ensure_future(self._save())

        container.add(open_button, save_button, self._get_element('status'))
        return container

    def _account_control(self):
        """
        The signed-in indicator for the header bar.

        Lives apart from the file controls: whether you are signed in is a
        property of the whole app, so it belongs in the title bar rather than
        buried in whichever tab happens to be open.
        """
        account = Div(style=dict(ACCOUNT_STYLE))
        if not self.configured:
            account.style.display = "none"
            return account

        label = self._register_element(
            'account_label', Span("", style=ACCOUNT_LABEL_STYLE))
        button = self._register_element(
            'account_button',
            Button("Sign in with Google", style=dict(ACCOUNT_BUTTON_STYLE)))

        def hover(active):
            # antioch's style proxy takes underscore names, not CSS hyphens.
            button.style.background_color = (
                ACCOUNT_BUTTON_HOVER if active else "transparent")

        button.on_mouseenter(lambda e: hover(True))
        button.on_mouseleave(lambda e: hover(False))

        @when(button.events.click)
        def on_click(sender, *args):
            asyncio.ensure_future(
                self._sign_out() if self.session.signed_in else self._sign_in())

        account.add(label, button)
        return account

    @property
    def account_element(self):
        """The header-bar control; an empty hidden Div when not configured."""
        return self._get_element('account')

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- status

    def _set_status(self, message, is_error=False):
        if not self.configured:
            return
        status = self._get_element('status')
        status.set_text(message)
        status.style.color = ERROR_COLOR if is_error else STATUS_STYLE["color"]

    def _fail(self, error):
        self._set_status(f"Error: {error}", is_error=True)
        self._fire_event('error', str(error))

    def _sync_buttons(self):
        signed_in = self.session.signed_in
        # Being signed in is not enough: the Drive scope is granted separately.
        usable = signed_in and self.session.has_drive_access
        self._get_element('account_button').set_text(
            "Sign out" if signed_in else "Sign in with Google")
        self._get_element('account_label').set_text(
            (self._email or "Signed in") if signed_in else "")
        for name in ('open', 'save'):
            self._get_element(name).set_disabled(not usable)
        self._fire_event('sign_in_change', usable)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ auth

    async def _sign_in(self):
        button = self._get_element('account_button')
        button.set_text("Signing in…")
        self._get_element('account_label').set_text("")
        try:
            await self.session.sign_in()
            # Display only; a failure here leaves the status reading
            # "Signed in", which is still true.
            self._email = await self.session.account_email()
            self._set_status(
                "" if self.session.has_drive_access else NO_DRIVE_MESSAGE,
                is_error=not self.session.has_drive_access)
        except Exception as error:
            # A cancelled popup is the common case here and is not a fault, so
            # it reads as a plain status rather than an error.
            self._email = None
            self._set_status("Sign-in cancelled."
                             if _was_cancelled(error) else f"Error: {error}")
        finally:
            self._sync_buttons()

    async def _sign_out(self):
        self.session.sign_out()
        self._email = None
        self._set_status("Signed out.")
        self._sync_buttons()

    async def restore(self):
        """
        Re-attach a previous session on page load, without prompting.

        Runs in the background after the app is up: it needs a network round
        trip for Google's script, and nothing else should wait on it.
        """
        if not self.configured:
            return False
        button = self._get_element('account_button')
        button.set_text("Restoring…")
        try:
            if not await self.session.restore():
                return False
            self._email = await self.session.account_email()
            if not self.session.has_drive_access:
                self._set_status(NO_DRIVE_MESSAGE, is_error=True)
            return True
        except Exception:
            # A failed restore is an ordinary outcome, not an error worth
            # showing: the user just sees the sign-in button.
            return False
        finally:
            self._sync_buttons()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ open

    async def _open(self):
        button = self._get_element('open')
        button.set_loading(True)
        try:
            self._require_drive()
            # Google's picker renders in its own iframe and can take a few
            # seconds; without this the button just sits there looking stuck.
            self._set_status("Opening Google Drive…")
            picked = await self.session.pick_file(PICKABLE)
            if picked is None:
                self._set_status("")
                return
            # Fired only now: the overlay must not cover Google's picker,
            # which the user is still interacting with until this point.
            self._fire_event('load_start', picked["name"])
            self._set_status(f"Opening {picked['name']}…")
            name, content = await self.client.download(
                picked["id"], picked["mimeType"])
            rows = parse_file(name, content)
            self._set_status(f"Loaded {len(rows)} rows from {name}")
            self._fire_event('data_loaded', rows, name)
        except Exception as error:
            self._fail(error)
        finally:
            button.set_loading(False)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ save

    async def _save(self):
        rows = list(self._get_rows() if self._get_rows else [])
        if not rows:
            self._set_status("Nothing to save — the spreadsheet is empty.")
            return

        try:
            self._require_drive()
        except Exception as error:
            self._fail(error)
            return

        choice = await self.dialog.ask(DEFAULT_SAVE_NAME)
        if choice is None:
            return
        name = choice["name"]
        if not name.lower().endswith(".csv"):
            name += ".csv"

        button = self._get_element('save')
        button.set_loading(True)
        self._set_status(f"Saving {name}…")
        try:
            result = await self.client.upload(
                name, rows_to_csv(rows), folder_id=choice["folder_id"])
            self._set_status(
                f"Saved {result.get('name', name)} to {choice['folder_name']}.")
        except Exception as error:
            self._fail(error)
        finally:
            button.set_loading(False)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------- for the plots

    def _require_drive(self):
        """
        Raise before a call that is certain to 403.

        The gallery's save buttons exist as soon as Drive is configured, so
        they can be clicked while signed out or without the Drive scope.
        """
        if not self.session.signed_in:
            raise RuntimeError("Sign in with Google first.")
        if not self.session.has_drive_access:
            raise RuntimeError(NO_DRIVE_MESSAGE)

    async def save_bytes(self, filename, data, mime_type):
        """
        Upload an already-built payload, e.g. a plot's SVG or zip.

        Asks for a name and destination first, exactly as the spreadsheet save
        does, so a graph does not silently land in the root of My Drive.
        """
        self._require_drive()
        choice = await self.dialog.ask(filename)
        if choice is None:
            return None
        result = await self.client.upload(
            choice["name"], data, mime_type=mime_type,
            folder_id=choice["folder_id"])
        self._set_status(
            f"Saved {result.get('name', choice['name'])} "
            f"to {choice['folder_name']}.")
        return result


def _was_cancelled(error):
    text = str(error).lower()
    return "popup" in text or "cancel" in text or "closed" in text

"""Choices the wizards offer, and the constants the builders share."""

# Intersample comparison metrics from sed_stats.metrics.

# shared grid, or the corresponding CDFs (ks/kuiper compare CDF curves).

    "similarity": {"label": "Similarity", "func": metrics.similarity, "input": "pdf",
                   "note": "0–1, higher is more similar"},
    "likeness": {"label": "Likeness", "func": metrics.likeness, "input": "pdf",
                 "note": "0–1, higher is more similar"},

           "note": "0–1, lower is more similar"},
    "kuiper": {"label": "Kuiper statistic", "func": metrics.kuiper, "input": "cdf",
               "note": "0–1, lower is more similar"},
}

    "non_metric": "Non-metric MDS",

}

# a sample with three times the analyses would otherwise pull the axis three
# times as hard, which is an artefact of how much was measured rather than
# anything about the rocks.
GRAIN_WEIGHTINGS = {
    "sample": "Every sample equally",
    "grain": "Every grain equally",
}

# Two-dimensional measures, Sundell & Saylor (2021) eqs 15-20. Unlike the 1D

BIVARIATE_METRICS = {

    "2": "2σ (95% confidence)",
}

# many standard deviations of padding so the widest kernel's tails fit.

# --------------------------------------------------------------- Google Drive
#
# Fill these in from a Google Cloud project to switch on "Sign in with Google".
# While any of them is blank the Drive controls stay hidden, so an unconfigured
# copy of the app simply has no Google features rather than a broken button.
#
# To get them (https://console.cloud.google.com/):

"""The Mixture model tool's output: unmixing a sink sample into its sources."""
import math

from antioch.elements import Div, P

from plot_lib import error_bar_trace, line_trace
from sed_stats import mixture

from .config import MIXTURE_METRICS
from .dataset import series_for
from .plots import make_plot
from .tables import result_table

CAPTION_STYLE = {"font-size": "13px", "color": "#555", "margin": "0 0 6px 0"}

TRIAL_COLOR = "rgba(0, 191, 214, 0.55)"
SINK_COLOR = "#1f4fd8"
CONTRIBUTION_COLOR = "#8e5b42"


def build_mixture(charts, rows, sample_col, dimension, opts):
    metric = opts["metric"]
    labels, series = series_for(rows, sample_col, dimension,
                                mixture.expected_form(metric), opts)

    sink_name = opts["sink"]
    sink = next((data for name, data in series if name == sink_name), None)
    sources = [(name, data) for name, data in series if name != sink_name]

    if sink is None:
        return P(f"The sink sample '{sink_name}' has no data for '{dimension}'.",
                 style={"color": "#6c757d"})
    if len(sources) < 2:
        return P("Need at least two source samples with data to unmix.",
                 style={"color": "#6c757d"})

    result = mixture.monte_carlo_model(
        sink_values=sink,
        source_values=[data for _, data in sources],
        source_names=[name for name, _ in sources],
        n_trials=opts["trials"],
        metric=metric,
    )

    return Div(
        _summary(sink_name, metric, opts["trials"], result),
        _top_trials_plot(charts, labels, sink, sink_name, dimension, result),
        _contribution_plot(charts, dimension, result),
        _contribution_table(metric, result),
    )


def _summary(sink_name, metric, trials, result):
    info = MIXTURE_METRICS[metric]
    return P(f"{trials:,} trials against {sink_name}, scored by {info['label']} "
             f"({info['note']}). Best of the top {len(result.top_scores)}: "
             f"{result.best_score:.4g}.", style=CAPTION_STYLE)


def _top_trials_plot(charts, labels, sink, sink_name, dimension, result):
    """The best model curves behind the sink they are trying to reproduce."""
    traces = []
    for i, line in enumerate(result.top_lines):
        traces.append(line_trace(
            labels, [float(v) for v in line],
            "Top trials" if i == 0 else f"Trial {i + 1}",
            color=TRIAL_COLOR, markers=False,
        ))
        # One legend entry stands for the whole bundle.
        traces[-1]["showlegend"] = i == 0
        traces[-1]["hoverinfo"] = "skip"

    # Added last so the sink draws on top of the bundle.
    traces.append(line_trace(labels, sink, sink_name, color=SINK_COLOR, markers=False))
    traces[-1]["line"]["width"] = 3

    y_title = "Probability"
    return Div(make_plot(charts, traces, f"{dimension} — top trials",
                         dimension, y_title,
                         filename=f"{dimension}_mixture_trials").element)


def _contribution_plot(charts, dimension, result):
    names = [c.name for c in result.contributions]
    values = [c.contribution for c in result.contributions]
    errors = [c.standard_deviation for c in result.contributions]

    trace = error_bar_trace(names, values, errors, "Contribution",
                            color=CONTRIBUTION_COLOR)
    return Div(make_plot(
        charts, [trace], f"{dimension} — relative contribution",
        "Source sample", "% contribution",
        height=460, show_legend=False,
        filename=f"{dimension}_mixture_contribution",
        extra_layout={
            "xaxis": {"title": {"text": "Source sample"},
                      "type": "category", "tickangle": -45},
            # Rotated sample names need room; the default 50px clipped them.
            "margin": {"l": 60, "r": 20, "t": 50, "b": 150},
        },
    ).element)


def _contribution_table(metric, result):
    body = [
        [c.name,
         "n/a" if math.isnan(c.contribution) else f"{c.contribution:.2f}",
         "n/a" if math.isnan(c.standard_deviation)
         else f"{c.standard_deviation:.2f}"]
        for c in result.contributions
    ]
    return Div(
        P("Relative contribution", style={**CAPTION_STYLE, "margin": "16px 0 6px 0"}),
        result_table(
            ["Source",
             f"% contribution ({MIXTURE_METRICS[metric]['label']})",
             "Standard deviation"],
            body,
        ),
    )
